Nia (People Ops): @channel important update: Emergency Family Leave + same-day PTO changes. Please read - short TL;DR then details.
Nia (People Ops): TL;DR: 1) Improved Emergency Family Leave intake (faster approvals + confidentiality lane). 2) Same-day PTO auto-approval for up to 2 days in a rolling 6-month window (manager notified). 3) New documentation options for urgent cases (manager attestation + post-hoc paperwork). Links: https://redwood-internal/hr/emergency-leave, https://redwood-internal/hr/same-day-pto
Nia (People Ops): Why: people were delayed getting time off during crises; managers worried about approvals when they couldn't be reached. These changes balance compassion with simple auditability.
Nia (People Ops): Key changes: - Emergency Intake: employees may request Emergency Family Leave via the portal or text the People Ops hotline. People Ops will create a confidential case and notify only the employee + their manager.
Nia (People Ops): - Same-day PTO auto-approval: for up to 2 unexpected partial or full days in any 6-month period, the system will auto-approve and notify the manager. If the manager objects within 48 hours, we'll triage. This prevents callers waiting for approvals.
Alex: Huge +1. For managers who are OOO, how will exceptions be handled?
Nia (People Ops): Manager Bot will receive the notification; if the manager is OOO or doesn't respond in 48h, People Ops steps in and confirms coverage. We won't revoke approved time retroactively.
Jia: What counts as "emergency"? Doctor emergency, school closures, funeral? Need clarity for consistency.
Nia (People Ops): Emergency definitions: serious illness/injury, immediate family death, sudden childcare loss, or other acute events preventing work. Minor appointments or planned care don't qualify. We included examples in the FAQ.
Sam: Paperwork anxiety: will post-hoc notes create problems for employees without medical docs?
Nia (People Ops): Good Q. For medical emergencies we accept manager attestation initially and request supporting docs within 30 days when feasible. Failure to provide docs may flag a review but won't automatically punish the employee; we'll reach out to discuss.
Payroll Bot: Note: Emergency Family Leave taken under this policy will be coded as EMERG_FAM_LEAVE (paid) up to 5 days per fiscal year; additional days may be unpaid or PTO. Payroll will process deductions/labels automatically.
Alex: Any impact to benefits or parental leave accruals?
Nia (People Ops): Short emergency leave does not affect long-term benefits accruals. For extended leaves, Benefits will coordinate and advise.
Nia (People Ops): Confidentiality: cases are limited-access; only People Ops, payroll (when needed), and the employee's manager see basic metadata. Sensitive docs are stored encrypted.
Jia: Can contractors use same-day PTO auto-approval?
Nia (People Ops): Contractors do not get paid Emergency Family Leave but managers can grant unpaid same-day time off. This auto-rule is for payroll employees only.
Nia (People Ops): Quick checklist (People Ops bot): 1) Employee submits emergency request or uses hotline 2) Manager notified 3) Auto-approval for same-day if within limit 4) People Ops creates case and requests docs if needed 5) Payroll codes time in next cycle. Link: https://redwood-internal/hr/checklist-emergency
Sam: Appreciate the faster lane. When is this effective?
Nia (People Ops): Effective immediately. We'll run a 30-min manager briefing next Tue 10am PT and record it. RSVP in the calendar invite.
Nia (People Ops): Thanks everyone. DM People Ops for unusual scenarios. End.
